is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. (An. arabiensis, An. gambiae M and S forms) in Niger.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports the Vgsc L995F (kdr-west) mutation.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 and Table 2 provide sample sizes and allelic frequencies for the kdr-w mutation by site, year, and collection method.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from 14 localities in Niger during the wet seasons of 2005, 2006, and 2007.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field data on kdr mutation frequencies in Niger.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study provides data for 14 specific localities (e.g., Firgoune, Garey, Banizoumbou, Zindarou, Maichilmi, Maikogo, Fararatt, Bermo, Tchake, Falenko, Damagaram, Guidimouni, Goudoumaria, Bosso) and Niamey.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study covers collections from 2005, 2006, and 2007.

duplicate_risk.evidence: This is a primary study reporting original data from a specific nationwide monitoring effort in Niger.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including sample sizes and frequencies, are provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study monitored the temporal and spatial distribution of the kdr-west (L995F) mutation in Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations in Niger following a nationwide LLIN distribution in 2005. The study analyzed 1,517 specimens collected across 14 localities over three years (2005-2007). Results showed a significant increase in kdr-w frequency in An. gambiae M forms following the LLIN implementation, while An. arabiensis remained susceptible.
